<!--
PURPOSE   Monthly record of one model's 12-month-ahead US recession probability:
          did the latest reading move, and how does it compare with the run-ups
          to past recessions? History is a walk-forward backtest; each later
          month is a live row appended by run_monthly.R and never rewritten.
SCOPE     Sign-constrained Ridge GLM only (TerraMetric-Atlas "Long-history
          subset" spec plus the U-6 − U-3 gap). Not TerraMetric-Atlas's
          blended headline.
PARAMS    log_path   — prediction log CSV (default ../log/predictions.csv)
          usrec_path — NBER recession indicator CSV (default ../log/usrec.csv)
          meta_path  — last run's data vintage + status (default ../log/meta.csv)
RENDER    quarto render report/recession_tracker.qmd   (from the repo root)
PREREQ    Rscript run_monthly.R   (fetches FRED, updates log/, renders this)
DEPENDS   R: readr, dplyr, lubridate, plotly, gt, htmltools; the repo's R/ modules.
          Reads only log/ — never fetches.
-->

```{r}
#| label: params
log_path   <- params$log_path
usrec_path <- params$usrec_path
meta_path  <- params$meta_path
```

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
for (f in sort(list.files("../R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE))) source(f)
source("_helpers.R")

lg <- read_log(log_path)
usrec <- read.csv(usrec_path, colClasses = c(date = "Date"))
lg <- lg[order(lg$month), ]

now <- latest_reading(lg)
met <- backtest_metrics(lg[lg$source == "backtest", ])
rt <- runup_table(lg, usrec)
last12 <- lg$prob[lg$month > now$month %m-% n_months(12)]
peak12_month <- lg$month[lg$month > now$month %m-% n_months(12)][which.max(last12)]
ago3 <- lg$prob[lg$month == now$month %m-% n_months(3)]
scored <- lg[!is.na(lg$rec_next12_actual), ]
base_rate <- mean(scored$rec_next12_actual)
alike <- scored$rec_next12_actual[scored$prob >= now$prob]
spans <- recession_spans(usrec, from = min(lg$month) %m-% n_months(24))
interp <- unique(lg[nzchar(lg$interpolated), c("month", "interpolated")])
meta <- read_meta(meta_path)
history <- model_history(log_path)
# A same-version rebuild (e.g. to add logged columns) archives too; only a
# different version is a model change
history <- history[history$version != MODEL_VERSION, , drop = FALSE]
drv <- driver_contributions(lg)
```

# 1 — Latest reading

```{r}
#| label: kpis
chg_col <- if (is.na(now$change_pts)) PAL$neutral else if (now$change_pts > 0) PAL$negative else PAL$positive
kpi_row(
  kpi_card("Recession probability (12m)", fmt_pct(now$prob), format(now$month, "%B %Y"), PAL$orange),
  kpi_card("Change", fmt_pts(now$change_pts),
           if (is.na(now$prev_month)) NULL else paste("vs", format(now$prev_month, "%B %Y")), chg_col),
  kpi_card("Data fetched",
           if (is.null(meta)) "—" else format(meta$fetched_at, "%d %b %Y"),
           "FRED vintage used for every row", PAL$neutral),
  kpi_card("Last 12 months", paste(fmt_pct(min(last12)), "–", fmt_pct(max(last12))), "range", PAL$navy),
  kpi_card("Logged", sprintf("%d months", nrow(lg)),
           sprintf("%d backtest · %d live", sum(lg$source == "backtest"), sum(lg$source == "live")), PAL$teal)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: headline-read
# Direction: ±5 pts over 3 months; level: elevated once 1.5× the base rate
chg3 <- if (length(ago3)) (now$prob - ago3) * 100 else NA_real_
trend <- if (is.na(chg3) || abs(chg3) < 5) "flat" else if (chg3 > 0) "rising" else "falling"
level <- if (now$prob >= 0.5) "high" else if (now$prob >= 1.5 * base_rate) "elevated" else "normal"
verdict <- switch(level,
  high = "The model puts a recession within 12 months at better-than-even odds.",
  elevated = paste("Recession risk is above normal", switch(trend,
    rising = "and climbing, the pattern seen before past recessions.",
    flat = "but holding steady rather than building.",
    falling = "but easing.")),
  normal = paste("Recession risk is near its long-run norm", if (trend == "rising") "but picking up." else "."))

peaks <- sprintf("%s %s", rt$recession, fmt_pct(rt$runup_peak, 0))
above <- rt$recession[now$prob >= rt$runup_peak]
below <- rt$recession[now$prob < rt$runup_peak]
after_peak <- usrec$recession[usrec$date > peak12_month]
li <- function(head, body) sprintf("<li><b>%s.</b> %s</li>", head, body)

callout(
  if (level == "normal") "output" else "warn", "What today's reading means",
  paste0(
    "<p style='margin:0 0 6px;'><b>", verdict, "</b></p><ul style='margin:0;padding-left:18px;'>",
    li("Level", sprintf(
      "%s against a %s base rate (the share of months since 1985 with a recession in the following 12), about %.1f× normal. Of the %d past months that read %s or higher, %s were followed by a recession within 12 months.",
      fmt_pct(now$prob), fmt_pct(base_rate, 0), now$prob / base_rate, length(alike), fmt_pct(now$prob),
      fmt_pct(mean(alike), 0))),
    li("Direction", sprintf(
      "%s over 3 months%s. The last 12 months peaked at %s in %s%s.",
      fmt_pts(chg3), if (length(ago3)) sprintf(" (%s in %s)", fmt_pct(ago3), format(now$month %m-% n_months(3), "%b %Y")) else "",
      fmt_pct(max(last12)), format(peak12_month, "%b %Y"),
      if (length(after_peak) && !any(after_peak == 1)) "; no recession has followed so far" else "")),
    li("Past run-ups", sprintf(
      "In the 12 months before each recession the model peaked at %s. Today is %s%s.",
      paste(peaks, collapse = " · "),
      if (length(above)) paste("above the peak before", paste(above, collapse = ", ")) else "below every one",
      if (length(above) && length(below)) paste(" and below", paste(below, collapse = ", ")) else "")),
    if ("2020" %in% above) li("Note", "2020 was the COVID shock, which no model on these inputs could see coming, so clearing its bar means little.") else "",
    "</ul>"
  )
)
```

# 2 — History

## 2.1 Probability and its drivers

**Top panel:** the monthly probability from `r format(min(lg$month), "%Y")`. The navy line is the
walk-forward backtest and orange points are live monthly readings. Shaded bands are NBER recessions.

**Bottom panel:** what is behind each reading. Each bar is one predictor's push on the model's
log-odds, measured from a neutral month where every predictor sits at its training median. Bars
above zero raise recession risk and bars below lower it. Together they make up the gap between that
month's reading and a neutral one. As a rough scale, a push of +0.7 doubles the odds of a recession.

```{r}
#| label: history-chart
#| fig-height: 8
# Shapes go on each panel before subplot(): layout(shapes =) applied after
# subplot() is dropped at build. Panel-level "paper" refs map to that panel.
bands <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(spans)), function(i) list(
  type = "rect", xref = "x", yref = "paper", layer = "below", line = list(width = 0),
  x0 = spans$start[i], x1 = spans$end[i] %m+% n_months(1), y0 = 0, y1 = 1, fillcolor = PAL$band
))
line50 <- list(
  type = "line", xref = "paper", x0 = 0, x1 = 1, y0 = 50, y1 = 50,
  line = list(color = PAL$neutral, dash = "dash", width = 1)
)
bt <- lg[lg$source == "backtest", ]
lv <- lg[lg$source == "live", ]

p <- plotly::plot_ly() |>
  plotly::add_lines(data = bt, x = ~month, y = ~ prob * 100, name = "Backtest",
                    line = list(color = PAL$navy, width = 1.6),
                    hovertemplate = "%{x|%b %Y}: %{y:.1f}%<extra>backtest</extra>")
if (nrow(lv)) {
  p <- p |> plotly::add_markers(data = lv, x = ~month, y = ~ prob * 100, name = "Live",
                                marker = list(color = PAL$orange, size = 7),
                                hovertemplate = "%{x|%b %Y}: %{y:.1f}%<extra>live</extra>")
}
p <- p |>
  plotly::add_annotations(x = now$month, y = now$prob * 100, text = fmt_pct(now$prob),
                          showarrow = TRUE, arrowcolor = PAL$orange, ax = 30, ay = -30,
                          font = list(color = PAL$orange, size = 13)) |>
  plotly::layout(shapes = c(bands, list(line50)))

pd <- plotly::plot_ly() |> plotly::layout(shapes = bands)
for (k in PREDICTORS) {
  pd <- pd |> plotly::add_bars(x = drv$month, y = drv[[k]], name = DRIVER_LABEL[[k]],
                               marker = list(color = DRIVER_COLOR[[k]], line = list(width = 0)),
                               hovertemplate = sprintf("%%{y:+.2f}<extra>%s</extra>", DRIVER_LABEL[[k]]))
}

plotly::subplot(p, pd, nrows = 2, shareX = TRUE, heights = c(0.55, 0.45), titleY = TRUE, margin = 0.04) |>
  tm_layout(yaxis = list(title = "Probability (%)", range = c(0, 100)),
            yaxis2 = list(title = "Push on log-odds", gridcolor = "#e9ecef",
                          zeroline = TRUE, zerolinecolor = PAL$navy, zerolinewidth = 1),
            barmode = "relative", bargap = 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: drivers-now
d_now <- unlist(drv[drv$month == now$month, PREDICTORS])
ups <- sort(d_now[d_now > 0.005], decreasing = TRUE)
downs <- sort(d_now[d_now < -0.005])
zeros <- PREDICTORS[unlist(lg[lg$month == now$month, paste0("b_", PREDICTORS)]) == 0]
push <- function(v) paste(sprintf("%s (%+.2f)", tolower(DRIVER_LABEL[names(v)]), v), collapse = ", ")
callout("note", sprintf("What is behind %s", format(now$month, "%B %Y")), paste0(
  if (length(ups)) paste0("Pushing risk up: ", push(ups), ". ") else "Nothing is pushing risk up. ",
  if (length(downs)) paste0("Pulling it down: ", push(downs), ". ") else "",
  sprintf("With every predictor at its training median the model would read %s, against %s now.",
          fmt_pct(plogis(drv$b0[drv$month == now$month])), fmt_pct(now$prob)),
  if (length(zeros)) sprintf(" %s %s a zero coefficient in the current fit, so %s nothing.",
                             paste(DRIVER_LABEL[zeros], collapse = " and "),
                             if (length(zeros) > 1) "have" else "has",
                             if (length(zeros) > 1) "they add" else "it adds") else ""
))
```

## 2.2 What moved the reading

**How to read this table.** Each column compares the latest month with an earlier one, shown in the
column header. Each row is how many percentage points of that change came from one predictor.
Positive numbers (red) pushed risk up and negative numbers (green) pulled it down. **Model refit**
is what re-estimating the model did with the data held fixed: the backtest refits every January
and live readings refit every month. The rows add up to **Total**, the change in the headline
reading.

```{r}
#| label: drivers-change
lags <- c(1, 3, 12)
earlier <- do.call(c, lapply(lags, function(k) now$month %m-% n_months(k)))
chg <- lapply(earlier, function(m) driver_change(lg, m, now$month))
ok <- !vapply(chg, is.null, logical(1))
x_now <- unlist(lg[lg$month == now$month, PREDICTORS])

tbl_d <- data.frame(
  driver = c(DRIVER_LABEL[PREDICTORS], "Model refit", "Total"),
  latest = c(sprintf(DRIVER_FMT[PREDICTORS], x_now), "", fmt_pct(now$prob)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
col_ids <- sprintf("m%d", lags)
for (i in seq_along(lags)) {
  tbl_d[[col_ids[i]]] <- if (ok[i]) c(chg[[i]]$pts, sum(chg[[i]]$pts)) else NA_real_
}
labels <- setNames(lapply(seq_along(lags), function(i) {
  p0 <- lg$prob[lg$month == earlier[i]]
  gt::html(sprintf("vs %s<br><span style='font-weight:400;'>%s</span>", format(earlier[i], "%b %Y"),
                   if (length(p0)) fmt_pct(p0) else "not scored"))
}), col_ids)

g <- gt::gt(tbl_d) |>
  gt::cols_label(.list = c(list(driver = "Predictor", latest = format(now$month, "Latest · %b %Y")), labels)) |>
  gt::tab_spanner("Change in probability (percentage points)", gt::all_of(col_ids)) |>
  gt::fmt_number(gt::all_of(col_ids), decimals = 1, force_sign = TRUE) |>
  gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "—") |>
  gt::cols_align("right", c("latest", gt::all_of(col_ids)))
for (cid in col_ids) {
  g <- g |>
    gt::tab_style(gt::cell_text(color = PAL$negative), gt::cells_body(gt::all_of(cid), rows = which(tbl_d[[cid]] >= 0.05))) |>
    gt::tab_style(gt::cell_text(color = PAL$positive), gt::cells_body(gt::all_of(cid), rows = which(tbl_d[[cid]] <= -0.05)))
}
g |>
  gt::tab_style(gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"), gt::cells_body(rows = driver == "Total")) |>
  gt::tab_style(gt::cell_borders(sides = "top", color = PAL$navy, weight = gt::px(2)),
                gt::cells_body(rows = driver == "Total")) |>
  gt::tab_options(column_labels.background.color = "#f1f3f5", table.width = gt::pct(100))
```

Each predictor's share of a change is exact on the log-odds scale. Turning it into percentage points
shares the move out in proportion, because the logistic curve is not a straight line. The rows
still add up to the total exactly.

# 3 — Compared with past run-ups

**How to read this table.** Each row is a past recession, labelled by the year it began. The first
pair of columns shows the model's highest and average monthly reading in the **12 months before**
that recession started, when it was still ahead. The bold bottom row runs the same calculation
on the latest 12 months. If today's numbers fall in the range of the rows above, the model's
recent readings look like a past pre-recession run-up.

```{r}
#| label: runup-table
today <- data.frame(
  recession = sprintf("Today · last 12 months to %s", format(now$month, "%b %Y")),
  runup_peak = max(last12), runup_mean = mean(last12), spell_peak = NA_real_, spell_mean = NA_real_
)
tbl <- rbind(rt, today)
gt::gt(tbl) |>
  gt::cols_label(recession = "Recession (start year)", runup_peak = "Peak", runup_mean = "Mean",
                 spell_peak = "Peak", spell_mean = "Mean") |>
  gt::tab_spanner("12 months before · compare with today", c(runup_peak, runup_mean)) |>
  gt::tab_spanner("Incl. the recession itself · reference only", c(spell_peak, spell_mean)) |>
  gt::fmt_percent(c(runup_peak, runup_mean, spell_peak, spell_mean), decimals = 0) |>
  gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "—") |>
  gt::tab_style(gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"), gt::cells_body(rows = nrow(tbl))) |>
  gt::tab_style(gt::cell_borders(sides = "top", color = PAL$navy, weight = gt::px(2)),
                gt::cells_body(rows = nrow(tbl))) |>
  gt::tab_options(column_labels.background.color = "#f1f3f5", table.width = gt::pct(100))
```

Today's row still includes the `r fmt_pct(max(last12), 0)` peak from `r format(peak12_month, "%b %Y")`.
The latest reading is `r fmt_pct(now$prob, 0)`. Section 1 shows which way it is moving.

The reference columns run from 12 months before each recession *through the recession itself*, so
their numbers are higher, because the model's strongest readings usually arrive once a recession has
already started. They match the Rolling Backtest panel in TerraMetric-Atlas. Today has no equivalent
because no recession is under way.

# 4 — Model notes

## 4.1 Specification

```{r}
#| label: spec
callout("logic", "In one line",
  paste0("A Ridge logistic regression of “recession in the next 12 months” on seven monthly macro ",
         "indicators. Each coefficient is held to the sign economic theory expects, and the model is ",
         "refitted on a rolling 30-year window using only outcomes already known at the time. ",
         "Version <code>", MODEL_VERSION, "</code>."))
```

### Inputs

**Target.** Month $t$ is labelled 1 if any of the next 12 months is an NBER recession month
([USREC](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/USREC)):

$$
R_t = \mathbb{1}\Big\{\textstyle\sum_{h=1}^{12} \text{USREC}_{t+h} > 0\Big\}
$$

The label is known once at least 6 of those 12 months have been observed.

**Predictors.** All seven come from FRED at monthly frequency. Daily series are averaged over the month.

| Predictor | Construction at month $t$ | FRED source | Expected sign of $\beta$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yield curve | $\text{spread}_t = \text{T10Y2Y}_t$, or $\text{DGS10}_t - \text{DGS2}_t$ where T10Y2Y is missing (pp) | [T10Y2Y](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/T10Y2Y), [DGS10](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10), [DGS2](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2) | $-$: a steeper curve means less risk |
| Unemployment rise | $\Delta u_t = u_t - \min_{0 \le j \le 11} u_{t-j}$ (pp above the 12-month low) | [UNRATE](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE) | $+$ |
| Underemployment gap rise | $\Delta g_t = g_t - \min_{0 \le j \le 11} g_{t-j}$, with $g = \text{U-6} - u$ (pp above the 12-month low) | [U6RATE](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/U6RATE), [UNRATE](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE) | $+$: more involuntary part-time and marginally attached workers means more risk |
| Payroll momentum | $\text{pay}_t = \tfrac{1}{3}\sum_{j=0}^{2} \left(N_{t-j} - N_{t-j-1}\right)$ (thousand jobs per month) | [PAYEMS](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/PAYEMS) | $-$ |
| Real fed funds rate | $r_t = i_t - 100\left(P_t / P_{t-12} - 1\right)$ (pp) | [FEDFUNDS](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FEDFUNDS), [CPIAUCSL](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL) | $+$: tighter policy means more risk |
| Prime-age participation | $\text{lfpr}_t$: participation rate, ages 25–54, level (%) | [LNS11300060](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/LNS11300060) | $-$ |
| Sentiment change | $\Delta_{12} s_t = S_t - S_{t-12}$ (index points) | [UMCSENT](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UMCSENT) | $-$: falling sentiment means more risk |

Here $u$ is the unemployment rate, $N$ total nonfarm payrolls, $i$ the effective fed funds rate,
$P$ headline CPI and $S$ the University of Michigan sentiment index. Every lag is by calendar month.
In the level series, a single missing month is filled log-linearly (see 4.3). The yield-curve
series and USREC are never filled.

U-6 starts in January 1994. Before then the gap is missing and scores as its training median
($z = 0$), so it adds nothing to those readings; fits whose window holds no U-6 data give it a
zero coefficient. From 1994 on, a month without U-6 is not scored.

### How it is applied

**Scaling.** Each predictor $x_{k}$ is robust-scaled using the median and MAD of the training
window, then clipped at ±3 so one extreme month cannot dominate:

$$
z_{k,t} = \operatorname{clip}\!\left(\frac{x_{k,t} - \operatorname{med}_{\mathcal{T}}(x_k)}{\operatorname{MAD}_{\mathcal{T}}(x_k)},\,-3,\,3\right)
$$

**Model.** A logistic link on the seven scaled predictors:

$$
\Pr(R_t = 1 \mid z_t) = \Lambda\!\left(\beta_0 + \beta_{\text{spread}}\, z^{\text{spread}}_t + \beta_{u}\, z^{\Delta u}_t
+ \beta_{g}\, z^{\Delta g}_t + \beta_{\text{pay}}\, z^{\text{pay}}_t + \beta_{r}\, z^{r}_t + \beta_{\text{lfpr}}\, z^{\text{lfpr}}_t
+ \beta_{\text{sent}}\, z^{\Delta s}_t\right),
\qquad \Lambda(v) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-v}}
$$

**Estimation.** Penalised maximum likelihood with a Ridge (L2) penalty, subject to theory-sign
constraints:

$$
\hat\beta(\lambda) = \arg\min_{\beta_0,\,\beta}\;
-\frac{1}{|\mathcal{T}|}\sum_{s \in \mathcal{T}} \Big[ R_s\,\eta_s - \log\!\left(1 + e^{\eta_s}\right) \Big]
+ \frac{\lambda}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{7} \beta_k^2,
\qquad \eta_s = \beta_0 + z_s^{\top}\beta
$$

$$
\text{s.t.}\quad \beta_{\text{spread}} \le 0,\;\; \beta_{u} \ge 0,\;\; \beta_{g} \ge 0,\;\; \beta_{\text{pay}} \le 0,\;\;
\beta_{r} \ge 0,\;\; \beta_{\text{lfpr}} \le 0,\;\; \beta_{\text{sent}} \le 0
$$

A coefficient may be 0, so a predictor whose recent data contradict theory drops out instead of
flipping sign. The fit uses `glmnet` with `alpha = 0`, which also standardises $z$ internally before
penalising. $\lambda$ is chosen by 5-fold cross-validation on binomial deviance. The folds are
stratified by outcome and use a fixed seed, so reruns are identical. The **one-standard-error rule**
picks the largest $\lambda$ whose CV deviance is within one standard error of the minimum.

**Training window (walk-forward).** A model used at date $\tau$ is trained on

$$
\mathcal{T}_\tau = \text{the latest } 360 \text{ months } s \text{ with } s \le \tau - 12,\;
\text{complete predictors and a resolved label } R_s
$$

The 12-month embargo means no training label looks past the forecast date. The backtest refits
on 1 January of each forecast year and scores every month of that year. Each live reading refits
with $\tau$ set to its own month. No forecast is made if $\mathcal{T}_\tau$ has fewer than 60 rows
or fewer than 6 recession-ahead months.

### What it produces

$\hat p_t = \Lambda\big(\hat\beta_0 + z_t^{\top}\hat\beta(\lambda_{\text{1se}})\big)$: the probability that
at least one of the 12 months after month $t$ is a recession month. This is the number in the KPI
row and on the chart. Each term $\hat\beta_k z_{k,t}$ of the sum is that predictor's push, shown in
Section 2. The fitted $\hat\beta$, medians and MADs are logged with every month, so the split
always uses the exact model that produced the reading.

```{r}
#| label: model-history
if (nrow(history)) {
  callout("note", "Model changes",
    paste0("History was rebuilt after a model change. Earlier versions are archived in <code>log/archive/</code>: ",
           paste(sprintf("<code>%s</code> (replaced %s)", history$version, format(history$archived_at, "%d %b %Y")),
                 collapse = ", "), ". Their live readings are not on this chart."))
}
```

## 4.2 Backtest performance

```{r}
#| label: metrics
kpi_row(
  kpi_card("Brier skill", sprintf("%.2f", met$skill), "vs. forecasting the base rate", PAL$navy),
  kpi_card("AUC", sprintf("%.2f", met$auc), "ranking of risky vs. safe months", PAL$navy),
  kpi_card("Hit rate", fmt_pct(met$hit_rate, 0), ">50% with a recession ahead", PAL$teal),
  kpi_card("False alarms", fmt_pct(met$false_alarm_rate, 0), ">50% with no recession ahead", PAL$warning)
)
```

## 4.3 Caveats

```{r}
#| label: caveats
callout("warn", "Read these before relying on the history",
  paste0(
    "<ul style='margin:0;padding-left:18px;'>",
    "<li><b>Revised data.</b> History uses today's FRED values, not what was published at the time, ",
    "so it is somewhat more flattering than a true real-time record.</li>",
    "<li><b>NBER dating lag ignored.</b> Outcomes count as known 12 months later; in reality NBER ",
    "dates turning points 6–12+ months after the fact.</li>",
    "<li><b>GLM alone.</b> This is not TerraMetric-Atlas's headline, which blends the GLM with a ",
    "hand-tuned prior.</li>",
    if (nrow(interp)) paste0("<li><b>Interpolated inputs.</b> ",
                             paste(sprintf("%s (%s)", format(interp$month, "%b %Y"), gsub(";", ", ", interp$interpolated)),
                                   collapse = "; "),
                             " — single missing months filled log-linearly.</li>") else "",
    "</ul>"
  ))
```

<details><summary>Glossary</summary>

**Brier skill**
: 1 − (model Brier score ÷ Brier score of always forecasting the training base rate). Above 0 beats the base rate.

**AUC**
: Probability that a randomly chosen month with a recession ahead scores higher than one without. 0.5 = coin flip, 1 = perfect.

**Walk-forward**
: Each prediction comes from a model fitted only on data available at the time.

**Embargo**
: The 12-month gap between the last training label and the forecast month, so no training outcome overlaps the forecast.

**Recession ahead**
: Any NBER recession month in the next 12 months. This is what the model predicts (`rec_next12` in the code). It counts as known once at least 6 of those months are observed.

**Base rate**
: Share of scored months since 1985 with a recession ahead. A reading at the base rate means normal risk.

**Run-up**
: The 12 months before a recession starts.

**Log-odds**
: $\log\big(p / (1 - p)\big)$, the scale on which the model adds up its predictors. +0.7 roughly doubles the odds.

**Push (contribution)**
: One predictor's term $\beta_k z_k$ in the log-odds, measured from a month with every predictor at its training median.

**Model refit**
: The change in a reading from re-estimating the model on a newer training window, with the data held fixed.

**Underemployment gap**
: U-6 minus the headline unemployment rate: people working part-time for economic reasons plus those marginally attached to the labour force, as a share of the labour force.

**NBER**
: National Bureau of Economic Research, which dates US recessions (FRED series USREC).

</details>
